items.translatedQuestion: To avoid meeting the wrong group, missing a group, or failing to meet a group at all, what information should a local guide clarify when reading the tour reception plan?
items.translatedAnswer:
The local guide should pay attention to the following:
(1) The names and telephone numbers of the domestic tour operator's contact person and the national guide.
(2) The number of group members and their sex, names, and occupations.
(3) The service number, arrival time, and meeting point for the transport by which the group will arrive locally.
(4) For an inbound group, also learn the name of the tour operator in the place of origin and the tour leader; the group's foreign-language name or code; the visitors' nationalities, languages, and religious beliefs; and the group's entry and exit points.

items.translatedQuestion: What aspects of transportation tickets should a local guide check when receiving an inbound group?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Whether the group's transportation tickets to the next destination have been booked as planned, whether there have been any changes, and whether revised arrangements have been confirmed.
(2) Whether the group has return tickets.
(3) Whether international air tickets have been issued for domestic flights within the country.
(4) Whether the group's return air tickets have been reconfirmed.

items.translatedQuestion: How should a local guide prepare in terms of language and knowledge before joining a tour group?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Prepare commentary for the sightseeing and visits specified in the reception plan; foreign-language guides should also prepare how they will express it in the target language.
(2) For groups with specialized interests, prepare the relevant professional knowledge and vocabulary.
(3) Prepare to discuss current topics, major domestic and international news, and subjects that may interest visitors.
(4) Make detailed inquiries in advance about any attractions with which you are unfamiliar.

items.translatedQuestion: When meeting an inbound group at an airport or railway station, how should a local guide verify that it is the group they are assigned to receive?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Ask which country or region the group has come from, the names of the tour operators in the place of origin and in China, and the names of the tour leader and national guide.
(2) If the group has neither a tour leader nor a national guide, check the group name and number, country of origin, number and names of visitors, and the main itinerary with the group members.

items.translatedQuestion: As the local guide, deliver a standard welcome speech to the tour group.
items.translatedAnswer:
The speech should include:
(1) Welcoming the visitors on behalf of the local receiving travel service, the driver, and yourself.
(2) Introducing yourself and your organization.
(3) Introducing the driver.
(4) Sincerely expressing your wish to provide high-quality service.
(5) Wishing the visitors an enjoyable trip.

Sample welcome speech (for reference only):
Ladies and gentlemen, good morning!
Welcome to Guangzhou. My name is xxx, and our driver's name is xxx. I am a guide with the Guangzhou branch of China International Travel Service. We are honored to be your guides during your stay (or: We are very pleased to be with you while you visit our city). I expect that for most of you, this is your first visit to Guangzhou. We will do our best to make your stay here enjoyable, relaxing, and comfortable. If you are dissatisfied with anything about our work or the hotel service, please do not hesitate to tell us so that we can make improvements promptly. We look forward to your cooperation. I hope you enjoy your sightseeing here and have a wonderful time.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide include when introducing the local area to visitors?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) The introduction should cover the local climate, population, administrative divisions, social life, cultural traditions, local specialties, and history.
(2) At appropriate times, also describe the cityscape, its development, and important buildings, streets, and other features along the route.

items.translatedQuestion: After visitors have checked into the hotel, how should a local guide stay in contact with the tour group?
items.translatedAnswer: The local guide should note the room numbers of the tour leader, national guide, and group members, and give the national guide and tour leader ways to get in touch, such as the guide's room number and telephone number, so they can make contact promptly if needed.

items.translatedQuestion: If the tour leader or national guide proposes a minor change to the reception plan or asks to add a new sightseeing activity, how should the local guide respond?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Report the request promptly to the relevant department of the travel agency. Accommodate requests that are reasonable and feasible as far as possible.
(2) For activities that require an additional charge, explain this to the tour leader or visitors in advance and collect the fee in accordance with the applicable rules.
(3) If a request truly cannot be accommodated, explain the reasons fully and patiently.

items.translatedQuestion: When a tour group with checked baggage arrives locally, how should the local guide check the baggage?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Help the group gather its baggage in the designated area and remind visitors to check that their belongings are complete and undamaged.
(2) After checking the baggage with the tour leader and national guide, hand it over to the baggage handler and complete the handover formalities together.
(3) If any baggage is missing or damaged, help the affected visitor file a report for lost baggage or compensation with the relevant transportation provider.

items.translatedQuestion: Before visitors get off the vehicle to visit an attraction, what information should the local guide give them?
items.translatedAnswer: The local guide should explain and remind visitors to remember the tour vehicle's type, color, identifying mark, and registration number, as well as where it is parked and when it will depart.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide do regarding the tour leader's and visitors' travel documents?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) In general, the local guide should not keep the group's travel documents. If a visitor's document is needed to complete a procedure, return it immediately once it has been used.
(2) The day before departure from the destination, check your own belongings to make sure you have not retained any visitors' documents or tickets. If you have, return them immediately and verify them in person.
(3) Some hotels require the tour leader to leave their documents at the front desk when the group checks in. When the group checks out, remind the tour leader to retrieve them.
(4) Before an inbound group departs the country, remind visitors to have their passports and declaration forms ready for inspection by border control and customs.

items.translatedQuestion: How should tour guides prevent visitors from getting separated from the group?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Remind visitors to remember the name of the local receiving travel service, the vehicle number, and the hotel name; not to wander too far from the group while it is moving; and not to return to the hotel too late after staying out or going out on their own.
(2) During visits and sightseeing, regularly brief visitors on the itinerary and clearly tell them the meal times and locations, sightseeing route, meeting time and place, and parking location.
(3) Stay with the visitors and count the group frequently.
(4) The local guide, national guide, and tour leader should coordinate closely: the local guide leads at the front, while the national guide and tour leader bring up the rear.
(5) The local guide should hold visitors' attention with engaging commentary.

items.translatedQuestion: When a tour group checks into a hotel, what should the local guide explain to the visitors?
items.translatedAnswer: The local guide should tell the group where to find facilities such as the currency exchange, Chinese and Western restaurants, entertainment venues, shops, and public restrooms, and explain important points about checking in and staying at the hotel.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide do before, during, and after a meal for a tour group?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Before the meal, verify and confirm each detail with the restaurant, including the location, time, number of diners, meal standard, and any special requirements.
(2) During the meal, check on the group once or twice, answer visitors' questions, and supervise and assess the restaurant's service quality.
(3) After the meal, settle the bill with the restaurant strictly according to the actual number of diners and the agreed meal standard.

items.translatedQuestion: How should a local guide arrange the tour group's scheduled and optional entertainment activities?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) If an entertainment program is included in the itinerary, the local guide should accompany the group and introduce the program.
(2) For an optional activity not included in the itinerary, such as a performance or other entertainment that visitors wish to attend at their own expense, the local guide should generally assist but usually does not accompany them.
(3) If visitors are going to a large entertainment venue, remind them not to get separated and pay attention to their whereabouts and surroundings to prevent problems.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide do before a tour group leaves its hotel?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Gather and check baggage for dispatch. If the group has baggage to be checked, at the agreed time count it with the tour leader, national guide, and baggage handler, and inspect how it has been packed.
(2) Complete the hotel check-out. Unless there are special circumstances, the local guide should check out by noon.
(3) Assemble the group and board the vehicle. Before leaving, ask visitors whether they have settled their accounts with the hotel and ask them to return their room keys to the front desk. Once everyone is seated, carefully count the people present and remind visitors to check that they have not left anything behind.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide do on the way back to the hotel after a day's sightseeing?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) On the way back, review the day's visits and sightseeing; provide additional commentary if needed and answer visitors' questions.
(2) If the vehicle is taking a different route back to the hotel, give commentary on the scenery along the way.
(3) Before visitors get off, announce the schedule for that evening or the following day, including the departure time and meeting place.
(4) Remind visitors to take their personal belongings with them.
(5) The local guide should get off first, assist visitors as they leave the vehicle, and say goodbye.

items.translatedQuestion: When a tour group enters its destination country, what are the three border checks it must go through?
items.translatedAnswer: The three checks required for entry are health and quarantine inspection, travel-document inspection, and customs inspection.

items.translatedQuestion: To avoid a missed flight, train, or ship, what timing should a guide allow when taking a tour group to its departure point?
items.translatedAnswer:
The guide should ensure that the group reaches the airport, railway station, or port before the flight, train, or ship departs. The specific requirements are:
(1) For an international flight or a flight to a coastal city, arrive 2 hours in advance.
(2) For a domestic flight, arrive 1.5 hours in advance.
(3) For a train or ship, arrive 1 hour in advance.

items.translatedQuestion: What principles should a national guide follow when agreeing on the itinerary with the local guide?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) If the local guide revises the itinerary, the national guide should maintain the principle that the order of activities may be changed, but activities may not be omitted. Report the matter to the originating travel agency if necessary.
(2) If the local guide recommends optional activities at the visitors' own expense, the national guide should seek the views of all group members.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a national guide do at each destination on the tour?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Brief the local guide on the tour group's situation and assist the local guide.
(2) Monitor service quality at each destination and, as appropriate, offer suggestions and recommendations for improvement.
(3) Protect visitors' safety and prevent and handle various incidents.
(4) Advise visitors on shopping.
(5) Stay in contact with the next destination.

items.translatedQuestion: What role does a national guide play during a tour, and what responsibilities does the guide have?
items.translatedAnswer: The national guide represents the originating travel agency and should take part in the group's activities from beginning to end. The guide is responsible for coordinating every stage of the itinerary, supervising implementation of the reception plan, and coordinating the tour leader, local guide, driver, and other reception staff.

items.translatedQuestion: How should a national guide supervise and advise the group while it is shopping?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) If the local guide schedules too many shopping stops or extends shopping time, the national guide should raise the matter promptly.
(2) Remind visitors to pay attention to the quality and price of goods and to beware of counterfeit or inferior products being passed off as genuine or high-quality goods.
(3) When visitors in an inbound group buy expensive items, especially cultural relics, remind them to keep their receipts for inspection when leaving the country. When they buy Chinese patent medicines or Chinese medicinal materials, explain the relevant Chinese customs regulations.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a national guide do when a tour group arrives at a hotel?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Take the initiative in helping the tour leader complete the group's check-in.
(2) Ask the tour leader to allocate the rooms, keep a list of the room assignments, and exchange room numbers with the tour leader for contact purposes.
(3) Warmly guide visitors to their rooms.
(4) If the local guide is not staying at the hotel, the national guide should take full responsibility for looking after the group.
(5) Note the hotel's front-desk telephone number and how to contact the local guide in case they are needed.

items.translatedQuestion: What measures should a national guide take to monitor service quality at each destination?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) If the activities at a destination substantially repeat those at previous stops, suggest that the local guide make the necessary adjustments.
(2) If there are concerns about the local reception service—for example, accommodation, meals, or vehicles do not meet the standards in the original agreement; the local guide unilaterally reduces or cancels sightseeing activities, adds paid activities, or schedules too much shopping—raise them with the local guide in a constructive manner.
(3) If the service still does not improve, raise the matter directly with the receiving travel service and, if necessary, report it to the originating travel agency.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a national guide do when an inbound group is about to leave the country?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) At the end of the tour, remind visitors to take their belongings and travel documents.
(2) Ask visitors for their opinions and suggestions about the reception service as a whole.
(3) Give a farewell speech, thank the visitors for their cooperation, and welcome them to visit again.

items.translatedQuestion: As the national guide, deliver a farewell speech to the tour group.
items.translatedAnswer:
The speech should include:
(1) Looking back on the tour and thanking everyone for their cooperation.
(2) Expressing friendship and the sadness of parting.
(3) Sincerely asking visitors for their opinions and suggestions about the reception service.
(4) If anything went wrong during the tour or any aspect of the service fell short of expectations, taking this opportunity to apologize to the visitors again.
(5) Offering warm wishes.

Sample farewell speech (for reference only):
Ladies and gentlemen,
Your visit to China is now coming to an end. Over the past 10 days, you have climbed the Great Wall, one of the Eight Wonders of the World, which is said to have been the only man-made object on Earth visible from the moon. You have visited the Forbidden City in Beijing, home to the emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties; and you have reviewed the ranks of the First Emperor of Qin in Xi'an—I mean the more than 6,000 Terracotta Warriors dating back over 2,000 years. The beautiful karst scenery of Guilin has delighted your eyes, and you have just tasted some of the best Chinese food in Guangzhou.... In short, I think you now have some idea of what China is like. But China is a vast country, with an area of 9.6 million square kilometers, a population of 1.3 billion, and a history spanning nearly 5,000 years. A 10-day visit to China is like the Chinese saying, “a dragonfly skimming the water”: it can only give you a brief glimpse. So, if you can come again, you will gain a better understanding of this country. I look forward to seeing you in China again in the near future.

However, I know it is time for you to go home and be reunited with your families. As you prepare to leave, I want to say that I have had the pleasure of hosting a wonderful group of wonderful people. It has been my honor to spend the past 10 days with you. I know this trip could not satisfy every one of you, and there is much room for improvement in our work. We would therefore be very grateful for any comments or complaints you may have about our service.

Friends, you have been such a wonderful group, and I really do not want to say goodbye. So all I can say is, “See you again!” Take care, and I wish you a pleasant journey home!

items.translatedQuestion: How should a tour guide respond to visitors who are demanding or critical?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Listen carefully; do not accuse visitors of making unreasonable demands or offer hasty explanations before they have finished speaking.
(2) Respond with a smile; do not show irritation or answer rudely just because you hear something unpleasant.
(3) Explain patiently and factually when a reasonable request cannot be fulfilled. Do not reject it outright by simply saying, “It can't be done.”

items.translatedQuestion: What kind of relationship should a tour guide maintain with visitors throughout a tour?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) The guide should remember that they are the host: be warm and hospitable, show generosity, and be accommodating toward visitors.
(2) The guide should not become overly familiar with visitors, get involved in disputes within the group, or stir up discord among visitors. Treat everyone equally and do not show favoritism.

items.translatedQuestion: How should a local guide assist with and arrange meetings between inbound visitors and other people?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) If visitors—especially a professional tour group—meet with Chinese counterparts or officials, the guide may act as an interpreter when necessary. If another interpreter is present, the guide may listen without taking part.
(2) If visitors wish to meet relatives or friends living in China, the guide should help arrange the meeting. In general, the guide is not obliged to interpret.

items.translatedQuestion: How should a local guide confirm the tour vehicle before receiving a group?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Contact the motor-transport company to confirm the vehicle type, registration number, and driver's name and telephone number.
(2) Agree with the driver on the meeting point and provide the itinerary and specific schedule.

items.translatedQuestion: What items should a local guide prepare before joining a tour group?
items.translatedAnswer: Before joining the group, obtain enough city maps, admission tickets, meal settlement slips, and funds according to the group size, and bring all necessary items: the reception plan, guide's IC card, the travel service's badge, guide flag, group-identification sign, and so on.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide do while the tour group is traveling to an attraction?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Review the day's schedule.
(2) Provide commentary on the scenery along the way.
(3) Briefly introduce the attraction.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide explain to visitors in front of an attraction map?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Explain the sightseeing route, how long it will take, and the meeting time and place.
(2) Explain relevant points visitors should observe during the visit.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a local guide tell visitors at a meal featuring local specialties?
items.translatedAnswer: The local guide should introduce the ingredients and preparation of the specialty dishes, their related stories or anecdotes, and how to eat them.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a national guide do if a conflict arises between the tour leader and visitors?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) The national guide should not probe into the origins of their conflict.
(2) The national guide should not express an opinion or become involved in the dispute.
(3) If necessary, the national guide may help mediate their relationship.

items.translatedQuestion: During sightseeing, what should a national guide do to protect visitors' safety and prevent accidents?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) During sightseeing, observe the surroundings and keep an eye on visitors' movements. Assist the local guide in completing the commentary, and prevent visitors from getting separated or having an accident.
(2) Remind visitors to take care of their personal safety and belongings. If an unexpected incident occurs, rely on the local guide to handle it appropriately.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a national guide do when the group is traveling a long distance by plane, train, or ship?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) When traveling by plane, train, or ship, actively seek the cooperation of staff from the civil aviation, railway, or shipping authorities to jointly provide security and onboard services.
(2) During the journey, remind visitors to take care of their personal safety and belongings.
(3) Organize entertainment and look after visitors' meals and rest.
(4) Keep baggage claim checks and plane, train, or ship tickets and other documents safe, and hand them to the local guide upon arrival at the next stop.
(5) When traveling by train, ask the tour leader in advance to assign compartments and sleeping berths.

items.translatedQuestion: What should a national guide do when the tour group leaves each destination?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Remind the local guide in advance to confirm the departure tickets and the exact departure time.
(2) Assist the tour leader and local guide with departure arrangements.
(3) Keep the tickets and travel documents safe.

items.translatedQuestion: What mental preparation should a tour guide make before joining a tour group?
items.translatedAnswer:
(1) Be prepared for demanding and complicated work. A tour guide must not only provide warm service in accordance with normal procedures, but also be mentally prepared to serve visitors with special needs and to face and handle problems or incidents that arise during reception.
(2) Be prepared to face complaints and criticism. Guiding work is complicated and arduous. Sometimes, even after doing everything possible to serve a group warmly and attentively, a guide may still face visitors who are critical, complain, or find fault with the guide's work, and may even file a complaint. Guides should be psychologically prepared for this, remain calm and composed, and continue serving visitors willingly and without resentment.
